summary: Ma'aser of animals means giving every tenth new animal as holy. It applies everywhere and always. Sheep and goats count together, but cattle and sheep do not, and neither do animals from different years.

chunks.st: The mitzva of animal tithe is in effect both in Eretz Yisrael and outside of Eretz Yisrael,

chunks.en: when the Beis HaMikdash stands and when it does not,
chunks.st: in the presence of, i.e., in the time of, the Temple and not in the presence of the Temple.

chunks.en: for regular animals but not for holy animals.
chunks.st: It is in effect with regard to non-sacred animals but not with regard to sacrificial animals.

chunks.st: “And all the tithe of the herd or the flock, whatever passes under the rod, the tenth shall be sacred to the Lord” (Leviticus 27:32), indicating that with regard to animal tithe, all animals that are included in the term flock are one species.

summary: Animals that are close enough to each other are counted together for ma'aser. If they are too far apart, they are counted separately.

chunks.he: מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה מִצְטָרֵף כִּמְלֹא רֶגֶל בְּהֵמָה רוֹעָה.
chunks.en: Animals for ma'aser join together if they are as far apart as a grazing animal walks.
chunks.st: Animals subject to the obligation of animal tithe join together if the distance between them is no greater than the distance that a grazing animal can walk and still be tended by one shepherd.

chunks.en: And how far does a grazing animal walk?
chunks.st: And how much is the distance that a grazing animal walks?

chunks.en: Sixteen mil.
chunks.st: It is sixteen mil.

words.note: A mil is a bit more than half a mile.

summary: Animals that were bought or received as a gift do not need ma'aser. Brothers who share their father's flock must give ma'aser, unless they split it and then became partners again.

chunks.en: An animal that was bought, or given to him as a present,
chunks.st: One who purchases an animal or has an animal that was given to him as a gift

chunks.en: is free from ma'aser of animals.
chunks.st: is exempt from separating animal tithe.

chunks.en: Brothers who are partners, who must pay the kalbon,
chunks.st: With regard to brothers and partners, i.e., brothers who are partners in the inheritance of their father, when they are obligated to add the premium [bakalbon]
chunks.stMore: to their annual half-shekel payment to the Temple

words.note: A small extra coin added to the half-shekel.

chunks.en: are free from ma'aser of animals.
chunks.st: they are exempt from animal tithe.

chunks.en: If they split up and then became partners again,
chunks.st: How so? If they divided the inheritance between them and then reentered a partnership,

chunks.en: they must pay the kalbon and are free from ma'aser of animals.
chunks.st: they are obligated to add the premium and are exempt from animal tithe.

summary: Every animal goes into the pen to be counted for ma'aser, except for a few kinds. The Rabbis argue about what counts as an "orphan" animal.

chunks.en: All the animals go into the pen to be tithed,
chunks.st: All cattle, sheep, and goats enter the pen to be tithed,

chunks.en: except for a mixed breed,
chunks.st: except for an animal crossbred from diverse kinds, e.g., a hybrid of a goat and a sheep;

chunks.en: a treifah, one born through its mother's side,
chunks.st: a tereifa; an animal born by caesarean section;

words.en: and the one that comes out

chunks.en: one too young, and an orphan.
chunks.st: one whose time has not yet arrived, i.e., that is younger than eight days old, which is when animals become eligible for sacrifice; and an orphan.

chunks.en: What is an orphan?
chunks.st: And what is an orphan?

chunks.en: Any one whose mother died or was shechted when it was born.
chunks.st: It is any animal whose mother died or was slaughtered while giving birth to it and thereafter completed giving birth to it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua says:

chunks.en: even if its mother was shechted but her skin is still there,
chunks.st: Even if its mother was slaughtered but its hide exists
chunks.stMore: at birth, i.e., if the mother’s hide is present after the birth,

chunks.en: this is not an orphan.
chunks.st: this is not an orphan.

summary: Three times a year the animals are gathered to give ma'aser. The Rabbis argue about the dates, and about when the year for ma'aser of animals begins.

chunks.en: There are three gathering times for ma'aser of animals:
chunks.st: There are three times during the year designated for gathering the animals that were born since the last date for animal tithe:

chunks.en: close to Pesach,
chunks.st: Adjacent to Passover,

chunks.en: close to Shavuos,
chunks.st: and adjacent to Shavuot,

words.note: Literally "the gathering", a name for Shavuos.

chunks.en: close to Sukkos.
chunks.st: and adjacent to Sukkot. And those are the gathering times for animal tithe;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Akiva says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

chunks.en: Ben Azzai says,
chunks.st: Ben Azzai says the dates are:

chunks.en: on the twenty-ninth of Adar,
chunks.st: On the twenty-ninth of Adar,

chunks.en: on the first of Sivan,
chunks.st: on the first of Sivan, and

chunks.en: on the twenty-ninth of Av.
chunks.st: on the twenty-ninth of Av.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Shimon say,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say that the dates are:

chunks.en: on the first of Nisan,
chunks.st: On the first of Nisan,

chunks.en: on the first of Sivan,
chunks.st: on the first of Sivan, and

chunks.en: on the twenty-ninth of Elul.
chunks.st: on the twenty-ninth of Elul.

chunks.en: And why did they say the twenty-ninth of Elul
chunks.st: And why did Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say the twenty-ninth of Elul,

chunks.st: and why did they not say the first of Tishrei?

chunks.en: Because it is Yom Tov,

chunks.en: and we cannot give ma'aser on Yom Tov.

chunks.en: So they moved it earlier, to the twenty-ninth of Elul.
chunks.st: Consequently, they brought it earlier, to the twenty-ninth of Elul.

chunks.en: the first of Elul is Rosh Hashanah for ma'aser of animals.

summary: How ma'aser of animals is done: the animals go out one at a time, and every tenth is marked as holy. The mishnah teaches what counts and what happens if counted animals jump back in.

chunks.en: How does he give ma'aser?
chunks.st: In what manner does one tithe the animals?

chunks.en: He gathers them into a pen
chunks.st: He gathers them in a pen

chunks.en: and makes them a small opening,
chunks.st: and provides them with a small, i.e., narrow, opening,

chunks.he: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיוּ שְׁנַיִם יְכוֹלִין לָצֵאת כְּאַחַת,
chunks.en: so that two cannot come out at once,
chunks.st: so that two animals will not be able to emerge together.

chunks.en: and he counts with a stick:
chunks.st: And he counts the animals as they emerge:

chunks.en: one, two, three, four,
chunks.st: One, two, three, four,

chunks.en: five, six, seven, eight, nine.
chunks.st: five, six, seven, eight, nine;

chunks.en: The one that comes out tenth, he marks with red paint
chunks.st: and he paints the animal that emerges tenth with red paint

words.en: and the one that comes out

chunks.en: and says, "This is ma'aser."
chunks.st: and declares: This is tithe.

chunks.st: or if he counted the animals when they were prone or standing

chunks.st: these animals are tithed after the fact.

chunks.en: If he had a hundred and took ten,
chunks.st: But if he had one hundred animals and he took ten as tithe,

chunks.st: that is not tithe,

chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:

chunks.en: If one of the counted ones jumped back in among them,

chunks.st: all those in the pen are exempt

chunks.en: If one of the ma'aser animals jumped back in among them,
chunks.st: If one of those animals that had been tithed, i.e., designated as the tenth, jumped back into the pen among
chunks.stMore: the animals that had not yet been counted, creating uncertainty with regard to all the animals there which was the animal tithe,

chunks.en: they must all graze until they get a blemish,
chunks.st: all the animals must graze until they become unfit for sacrifice,

chunks.en: and the owners eat them with their blemish.
chunks.st: and each of them may be eaten in its blemished state by its owner once it develops a blemish.

summary: What happens if the animals come out two at once, or if a person mixes up the numbers when counting for ma'aser.

chunks.en: If two came out at once,
chunks.st: If two animals emerged as one,

chunks.en: he counts them two by two.
chunks.st: one counts them as twos,
chunks.stMore: i.e., as though they came out one after the other.

chunks.en: If he counted them as one, the ninth and the tenth are spoiled.
chunks.st: If he mistakenly counted two of the animals at the beginning or in the middle of the ten as one, and then continued his count, the ninth and the tenth are flawed,

chunks.he: יָצְאוּ תְּשִׁיעִי וַעֲשִׂירִי כְּאַחַת, תְּשִׁיעִי וַעֲשִׂירִי מְקֻלְקָלִין.
chunks.en: If the ninth and tenth came out at once, the ninth and the tenth are spoiled.
chunks.st: as he called the tenth: Ninth, and he called the eleventh: Tenth.

chunks.en: If he called the ninth "tenth," and the tenth
chunks.st: If he mistakenly called the ninth: Tenth, and the tenth:

chunks.st: Ninth, and the eleventh: Tenth,

chunks.en: all three of them are holy.
chunks.st: the three of them are sacred,
chunks.stMore: although each has a different halakhic status.

chunks.st: The ninth is eaten in its blemished state;

chunks.en: and the tenth is ma'aser,

chunks.en: and the eleventh is brought as a shelamim and makes a temurah.
chunks.st: and the eleventh is sacrificed as a peace offering, from which the breast and the thigh are given to the priest. And the eleventh renders a non-sacred animal that is exchanged for the peace offering consecrated as a substitute and he sacrifices it as a peace offering;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.en: "Can a temurah make a temurah?"
chunks.st: and does a substitute render another animal a substitute?
chunks.stMore: Everyone agrees that a substitute is created only in exchange for an originally consecrated animal.

chunks.en: They said in the name of Rabbi Meir,
chunks.st: The Sages said in the name of Rabbi Meir:
chunks.stMore: The eleventh animal is not considered a substitute for the animal tithe, since

chunks.he: אִלּוּ הָיָה תְמוּרָה, לֹא הָיָה קָרֵב.
chunks.en: if it were a temurah, it would not be brought as a korban.
chunks.st: if it were a substitute it would not be sacrificed,
chunks.stMore: as the substitute for an animal tithe is not sacrificed.

chunks.en: If he called the ninth "tenth,"
chunks.st: If one called the ninth animal: Tenth,

chunks.st: and the tenth: Tenth, and the eleventh: Tenth,

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.he: כֹּל שֶׁלֹּא נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם עֲשִׂירִי מִמֶּנּוּ,
